mainTopic: The end of the slave ברייתא on יום או יומים and קנין פירות, then how רב's demand that a married woman protest fits with the משנה that a husband has no חזקה on his wife's property
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about a slave who was sold while the seller kept the right to use him for thirty days. Which master gets the exemption of יום או יומים? רבי יוסי says both masters get it. He is unsure whether קנין פירות counts like קנין הגוף, and a ספק נפשות is judged leniently. רבי אלעזר says neither master gets it, and רבא explains from the words 'כי כספו הוא' that the master must fully own the slave. The גמרא then turns to the משנה that a husband cannot gain a חזקה on his wife's property. It challenges this with רב's statement that a married woman must protest, which seems to mean protesting against her husband. רבא answers that רב means a husband who dug pits, ditches and caves in her land. He defends this against the rule 'אין חזקה לנזקין' in two ways. רב יוסף instead says she protests against an outsider who used the field for three years after the husband died and is believed through a מיגו. The amud ends as the גמרא goes back to study רב's statement that no one can gain a חזקה on a married woman's property, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Both masters are covered by the rule of 'a day or two days'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that both the seller and the buyer of the slave are covered by the rule of יום או יומים. One is covered because the slave is under him, the other because the slave is 'his money'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them are included in the law of 'a day or two days'. This one, because the slave is under him, and that one, because the slave is his money.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא, and this is רבי יוסי's opinion. He says both masters of the slave get the exemption of יום או יומים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a slave who was sold, but the seller keeps the right to use him for thirty days. The seller is covered because the slave is 'under him' and serves him. The buyer is covered because he owns the slave, so the slave is 'his money'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A day or two days': a master who hits his slave is not put to death if the slave lives a day or two before dying
Under him, meaning the slave works for him
His money, meaning his property

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶם יֶשְׁנָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם –
phrases.english: Both of them are included in the law of 'a day or two days'
phrases.notes: From שמות 21:21: if the slave lives a day or two after being hit, the master isn't put to death.

phrases.english: This one, because the slave is under him,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the seller, who still gets to use the slave during the thirty days.

phrases.english: and that one, because the slave is his money

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵיהֶם יֶשְׁנָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, both the master who uses the slave and the master who owns him are covered by יום או יומים.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי exempts both: he is unsure, and capital cases go leniently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי. He is unsure whether owning the use of something (קנין פירות) counts like owning the thing itself (קנין הגוף). Since this is a ספק נפשות, we are lenient with both masters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is unsure whether ownership of the use and profits is like ownership of the item itself, or not like ownership of the item itself. And in a doubt about life and death, we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוסי can exempt both masters at once. He is unsure who the 'real' owner is, so he is lenient with both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose קנין פירות counts as ownership. Then the seller, who has the use of the slave, is the real master. Suppose it does not count. Then the buyer, who owns the slave itself, is the real master. Since we cannot tell which one it is, and the death penalty is at stake, neither master is put to death.

keyTerms.meaning: Owning only the use and profits of something
Owning the thing itself
When there is a doubt in a life-and-death case, we rule leniently

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of קנין פירות is the real issue behind אמימר's ruling about selling נכסי מלוג. This ברייתא is being brought to show where his view comes from.

phrases.english: And he is unsure

phrases.aramaic: אִי קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: whether ownership of the use and profits is like ownership of the item itself,
or not like ownership of the item itself,
and in a doubt about life and death, we are lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוסי's ruling in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because it is unclear whether קנין פירות equals קנין הגוף, both masters are exempt, since a ספק נפשות is judged leniently.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Neither master is covered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says neither master gets the exemption. The buyer lacks the slave being 'under him', and the seller lacks the slave being 'his money'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Both of them are not included in the law of 'a day or two days'. This one, because the slave is not under him, and that one, because the slave is not his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite view. According to רבי אלעזר, neither master is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that to count as the master, you need both: to own the slave and to have the use of him. Here each master has only half, so neither one is a full master.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not
Because he is not

steps.confusionAlert: Here the order is flipped from רבי יוסי. The first 'this one' is the buyer, who does not have the slave working for him. The second is the seller, who no longer owns the slave.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶם אֵינָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם –
phrases.english: Both of them are not included in the law of 'a day or two days'
This one, because the slave is not under him,
phrases.notes: This is the buyer. He owns the slave, but the slave is still working for the seller.

phrases.english: and that one, because the slave is not his money.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the master who uses the slave nor the master who owns him is covered by יום או יומים.

steps.title: רבא gives רבי אלעזר's source: 'his money' means fully his
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבי אלעזר's reason from the פסוק 'כי כספו הוא'. The word 'his money' means money that belongs only to him, so the master must fully own the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר? The verse says, 'He shall not be punished, for he is his money': his money, which belongs only to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source in the פסוק for רבי אלעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the slave 'his money'. רבא reads this as money that is completely his, with both ownership and use. A slave split between two people is not fully anyone's money, so neither master gets the exemption. This supports אמימר, who said that neither husband nor wife can sell נכסי מלוג.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
That belongs only to him

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר and רבא, you count as the owner only if you own the item and also have its use. This is the basis for אמימר.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?
The verse says:
'He shall not be punished, for he is his money'
his money, which belongs only to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אלעזר's view in step 3
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule that only a full owner counts as the master
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'כי כספו הוא' (שמות 21:21), read as 'his money that belongs only to him'

steps.title: The משנה: A husband cannot make a חזקה on his wife's property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a husband cannot gain a חזקה on his wife's property. This sets up a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a man does not have a חזקה in his wife's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up the next move, a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if someone uses land for three years without protest, he gets a חזקה, a presumption that he owns it. The משנה says a husband does not get a חזקה on his wife's land, since he has a right to use it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption of ownership that comes from using property openly for three years
His wife's property

phrases.english: And a man does not have a presumption of ownership in his wife's property.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband cannot establish a חזקה on his wife's property.

steps.title: Challenge from רב: A married woman must protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with רב's statement that a married woman needs to make a מחאה (protest).
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: A married woman must protest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב that seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A protest is only needed when someone could otherwise gain a חזקה. If a married woman must protest, it sounds as if someone can gain a חזקה on her property. The next steps work out who that someone is.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't רב say?
A married woman
To protest, so that the other person does not gain a חזקה

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
A married woman must protest!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב: אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ צְרִיכָה לְמַחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a husband cannot make a חזקה on his wife's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a married woman must protest, someone must be able to gain a חזקה on her property. The גמרא will argue that this someone is her husband.

steps.title: Against whom must she protest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom רב means: against whom must the woman protest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to sharpen the challenge. It is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two options: an outsider or her husband. The גמרא will rule out the outsider, which will leave the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Against whom? About whom?

phrases.english: Against whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies רב's statement to build the challenge
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the person against whom a married woman must protest

steps.title: It cannot mean an outsider, since רב says no one gains a חזקה on a married woman's property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רב meant an outsider. רב himself said that no one can gain a חזקה on a married woman's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say against another person: but didn't רב say that one cannot establish a חזקה on the property of a married woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, an outsider, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב has a second statement: outsiders can never gain a חזקה on a married woman's land. So she would never need to protest against an outsider, and רב's first statement cannot be about one.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Against someone else, an outsider
One cannot gain a חזקה

phrases.english: If you say against another person,
but didn't Rav say:
One cannot establish a presumption of ownership on the property of a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the first possible answer to step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רב's protest requirement is aimed at an outsider
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts רב's own rule that outsiders cannot gain a חזקה on a married woman's property

steps.title: So it must mean the husband, which contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The only option left is that she must protest against her husband. That means a husband can gain a חזקה, which goes against the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it against the husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. רב must mean the husband, so רב seems to argue with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she must protest against her husband, then without a protest the husband could gain a חזקה on her property. The משנה said a husband cannot gain one, so now there is an open contradiction for the גמרא to resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it?
Against the husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens the question about how strong a husband's rights in his wife's property are. The גמרא will need to explain how רב and the משנה fit together.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it against the husband?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 8 and completes the challenge begun in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a husband has no חזקה on his wife's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רב requires a protest and it cannot be aimed at an outsider, it must be aimed at the husband. That means a husband can gain a חזקה without a protest.

steps.title: רבא: רב means the husband, when he dug pits in her land
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the קשיא. רב really is talking about protesting against the husband, but only in a case where the husband dug pits, ditches and caves in the wife's field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, רב is talking about the husband. It is a case where he dug pits, ditches and caves in her land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the contradiction between רב and the משנה. רב's case is a husband who dug pits and caves in his wife's land, not a husband who just farmed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about normal use: a husband eats the fruits by right, so his use proves nothing. Digging pits and caves is not normal use, because it changes and damages the land. That acts like an owner, so she must protest, and if she stays silent he can gain a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Keeps the original idea while adding a detail.
Pits (cisterns dug into the ground)
Long, narrow ditches
Caves (covered underground spaces)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not disagreeing with the משנה. The משנה covers a husband's normal use of the land, and רב covers the unusual case of digging into it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, [Rav means] with regard to the husband,
and it is a case where he dug in it
pits, ditches, and caves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by narrowing רב's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רב is talking about a special case of unusual use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's need for a מחאה against the husband seemed to clash with the משנה that a husband has no חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about normal use of the land. רב is about a husband who dug pits, ditches and caves, which is owner-like behavior.

steps.title: Challenge: there is no presumption of ownership through damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ruling from רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: 'אין חזקה לנזקין', there is no חזקה for damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: There is no חזקה for damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer. Digging pits damages the land, and there is a known rule that damaging does not create a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the husband gains a חזקה because he dug pits, which is damage. But if damage never creates a חזקה, digging should help the husband even less than normal use does. So רבא's case seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't [so-and-so] say...?' Brings a source that contradicts what was just said.
A presumption of ownership, usually gained by using land for three years with no protest
Damages / damaging actions

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Naḥman say
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
There is no presumptive ownership for damage!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a husband gains a חזקה by digging pits in his wife's land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Digging pits is damage, and the rule is 'אין חזקה לנזקין'. So damage cannot be the thing that gives the husband a חזקה.

steps.title: Reread the rule: damage does not need the usual three years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the rule as 'אין דין חזקה לנזקין'. Damage is not under the normal three-year חזקה rule, because the damager gains a חזקה immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: the usual law of חזקה does not apply to damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the rule differently. It does not mean 'damage gives no חזקה.' It means 'damage does not follow the regular three-year rule.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you need three years of use to gain a חזקה. But an owner who sees someone damaging his land is expected to protest right away. If he stays silent, the damager gains a חזקה at once. So the husband who digs pits gains a חזקה very quickly, which fits רבא perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say' — read the statement this way instead
The standard law of חזקה (the three-year rule)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying damage never gives a חזקה. It says the opposite: damage gives one even faster, with no three-year wait.

phrases.english: Say: there is no [regular] law of presumptive ownership for damage.
phrases.notes: He means the three-year waiting time doesn't apply here, so the damager's חזקה works right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by rereading the words of the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין חזקה לנזקין' sounded like damage can never create a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means damage is not under the normal three-year rule, because the חזקה comes immediately.

steps.title: Second answer: the rule is about smoke and bathrooms, not land ownership
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the rule 'אין חזקה לנזקין' was explained by רב מרי as smoke and by רב זביד as a bathroom. It is about a neighbor's right to cause a nuisance, not about owning land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this: wasn't it said about that rule that רב מרי explained it as smoke, and רב זביד explained it as a bathroom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to remove the challenge. The rule 'אין חזקה לנזקין' is about a different subject entirely, so it says nothing against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי and רב זביד explain that the rule is about someone whose smoke or bathroom bothers his neighbors. Even if the neighbors stayed quiet for years, he never gains a permanent right to keep bothering them. That is a 'חזקה' to keep doing an activity, not a חזקה of owning a field. So it does not touch the husband who dug pits.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want, say...' Introduces a second, alternative answer.
'It was said about it' — a later explanation of an earlier statement
Smoke
A bathroom / outhouse (which gives off a bad smell)

steps.whatToRemember: A husband normally cannot gain a חזקה on his wife's land (the משנה). But if he digs pits, ditches or caves and she does not protest, he can, as רב says and רבא explains. The rule 'אין חזקה לנזקין' does not contradict this. Either damage gains a חזקה immediately, or that rule is only about smoke and bathroom nuisances.
steps.whyThisMatters: The word חזקה has two meanings: a presumption of owning property, and a set right to keep doing something that affects neighbors. Keeping these apart solves the challenge.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
Wasn't it said about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule 'אין חזקה לנזקין' from step 11.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: [it is about] smoke,
Rav Zevid said: [it is about] a bathroom?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the challenging source is about a different subject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין חזקה לנזקין' seemed to be about gaining ownership of land through damaging it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about nuisances like smoke or a bathroom, where staying silent never creates a permanent right. It is not about owning land.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's explanation stands: a husband who digs pits, ditches and caves in his wife's land can gain a חזקה if she does not protest.

steps.title: רב יוסף: She Protests Against an Outsider Who Has a מיגו
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב is talking about an outsider. That outsider used the field for part of the time during the husband's life and for three years after his death. He is believed, through a מיגו, when he claims he bought it from the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Really, רב means she must protest against another person. The case is where he used the field for part of a חזקה while the husband was alive, and for three years after the husband died. Since he could have said 'I bought it from you,' he is also believed when he says 'You sold it to your husband, and he sold it to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new way to answer the קשיא from step 9. He says the wife protests against an outsider, not against her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying she protests against the husband would let a husband gain a חזקה, which goes against the משנה. רב יוסף's outsider gets his three full years after the husband died, when she is no longer an אשת איש, so רב's rule from step 8 does not block him. Through a מיגו (he could have said 'I bought it from you'), he is believed when he says the husband sold it to him, so she needed to protest.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really: we keep the first idea after all
Against another person, an outsider who is not the husband
Part of the three-year period needed for a חזקה
Since he could have made a better claim, we believe the claim he did make
He is believed

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a second way, besides רבא's, to explain רב's rule without letting a husband gain a חזקה in his wife's property.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sales. He is not claiming he bought it from her. He claims she sold it to her husband and the husband sold it to him. The מיגו is what makes this weaker claim believable.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Actually, she protests against another person,
and the case is where he used the field for part of a חזקה
during the husband's lifetime,
and for three years after the husband's death;
since, if he wanted, he could have said to her:
"I bought it from you,"
so when he says to her instead:
"You sold it to him, and he sold it to me,"
he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the קשיא of step 9, offered instead of רבא's answer (steps 10-13).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) and using a מיגו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Protesting against an outsider seemed to make no sense, so it looked like רב must mean protesting against the husband, which would give the husband a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: She protests against an outsider who held the field three years after the husband's death. His claim of buying it from the husband is believed through a מיגו.

steps.title: Returning to רב's Rule on a Married Woman's Property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to look closely at רב's own statement: no one can gain a חזקה in a married woman's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רב said, one cannot gain a חזקה in the property of a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the word גופא to go back and quote רב's statement in full. This is a setup line, preparing to discuss the statement, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא only used this statement of רב as a source in the back-and-forth. Now it quotes the statement on its own so it can examine its details.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': returning to a statement that was quoted earlier, to study it directly
One cannot gain a חזקה (proof of ownership through use)
The property of a married woman

phrases.english: Now to the matter itself: Rav said:
One cannot gain a חזקה in the property of a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב: אֵין מַחְזִיקִין בְּנִכְסֵי אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the back-and-forth about whom she protests against, and returns to study רב's original statement directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one can gain a חזקה in a married woman's property.
